memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "At a lodging place on the way, the Lord met Moses and was about to kill him. But Zipporah took a flint knife, cut off her son's foreskin and touched Moses' feet with it. "Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me," she said. So the Lord let him alone. (At that time she said "bridegroom of blood," referring to circumcision.)" - Exodus 4:24-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is one of the strangest passages in the Bible, and honesty is better than pretending it is clear. Many details are genuinely uncertain, and careful scholars differ.

What we can reasonably say is this. Circumcision was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham, commanded on pain of being cut off from the people. It appears Moses had not circumcised his son — perhaps out of deference to his Midianite wife, who clearly found the practice distressing. And now the man about to lead the covenant nation is himself in breach of the covenant sign.

God takes this with deadly seriousness. Zipporah acts quickly, the covenant sign is applied, and Moses is spared.

The lesson is uncomfortable but important: God does not overlook disobedience in those He calls to lead. Public calling never excuses private neglect. James warns that teachers will be judged more strictly (Jas 3:1).

Notice also that Moses is spared through the shedding of blood. That thread runs right through Scripture to the cross, where blood was shed once for all.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an area of private disobedience I have allowed because my public life looks fine?
2. Do I take God's commands as seriously as He does?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, search my private life, not just my public one. Where I have quietly disobeyed, bring me to repentance. Amen.
